record.what_it_does: Cloud CRM for managing leads, contacts, deals, sales pipelines and workflow automation.
record.auth_notes: The API uses OAuth 2.0 only. Access tokens are valid for 1 hour. Refresh tokens last until the end user revokes them. Clients are registered in the Zoho API Console: server-based clients suit multi-user apps, and Self Client suits single-user backends. Zoho runs separate data centers, and the accounts and API domains differ by region (.com, .eu, .in, .com.au and others), so token and API calls must go to the user's own domain. The remote MCP servers also use an OAuth browser flow.
record.access_notes: The docs show no approval step for registering OAuth clients in the Zoho API Console. Every edition has a published API credit limit, including Free at 5,000 credits per 24 hours. Paid editions get 50,000 credits plus a per-user amount, capped at 100K for Standard, 3M for Professional, 5M for Enterprise and unlimited for Ultimate. Trial editions get the same limits as their paid editions. Zoho also offers a free Developer Edition with no expiry, for testing. Listing on the Zoho Marketplace is a separate step and is not required for API access.
record.api_breadth_notes: The V8 REST API has six groups: Metadata, Core (record CRUD across all modules, plus related records, notes, attachments, tags and users), Composite, Bulk read/write, Notifications, and Query (COQL). There are well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: Zoho hosts four pre-built CRM MCP servers on zohomcp.in: Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, and Workflow & Process Automation. One example is https://zoho-crm-data-operations-60065097786.zohomcp.in/mcp/<key>/message. Org-specific URLs are under Setup > Developer Hub > MCP for AI Agents. The servers use OAuth on first use and work with any MCP client; Zoho names Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf. Zoho also has a broader Zoho MCP console. CData, Pipedream and Workato offer third-party servers.
record.blocker_notes: There is no real blocker. The main engineering concern is handling multiple data centers: the accounts and API domains vary by region, so the toolkit must find the user's domain from the token response. Free-edition orgs get only 5,000 credits per day. Org-level CRM sandboxes need Enterprise or Ultimate, but the free Developer Edition covers testing.
